core_obligations: Descend a G-tilde-map to a G-map: since the action of pi_1(X) on X-tilde is free, the induced action on any cycle M-bar over X-tilde is free, so one may quotient by it and obtain a cycle M = M-bar/pi_1(X) over X with residual action of G = G-tilde/pi_1(X) (proof lines 516-520).

Lift a G-map to a G-tilde-map: pull back the covering X-tilde -> X along f : M -> X to get a pi_1(X)-covering M-tilde -> M, and pull back the G-tilde-action to M-tilde inside M x X-tilde by the stated formula, making the lifted map equivariant (proof lines 521-529).

Match the extra structure: verify that the same construction gives a bijection between G-invariant metrics on M and G-tilde-invariant metrics on M-tilde, and works for bordisms as well (proof lines 531-533).
Conclude: the two constructions are inverse to each other and preserve all the additional structure, hence induce the required isomorphism of exact sequences (proof lines 534-535).
proof_roadmap: Build the two inverse correspondences between equivariant cycles, first descending along the free pi_1(X)-action and then lifting by pull-back of the covering (proof lines 516-529).
Transfer the extra structure (metrics, bordisms) through the same construction and conclude the isomorphism (proof lines 531-535).
difficulty_reason: The proposition compares the G-equivariant Stolz exact sequence of a space X with the G-tilde-equivariant one of its covering X-tilde and claims they are isomorphic (statement lines 510-514). The proof constructs two inverse operations on equivariant cycles: descending a G-tilde-cycle by quotienting out the free pi_1(X)-action, and lifting a G-cycle by pulling back the covering and letting the group act on the fibre product inside M x X-tilde (proof lines 516-529). The step that carries the content is the lifting, because the G-tilde-action has to be defined on the pulled-back covering in such a way that the lifted map is equivariant, and the author writes that action down explicitly; the rest of the proof transfers metrics and bordisms through the same correspondence. The construction is elementary once the two group actions are set up correctly. H2.
